function.name: api_fetch
function.description: GET one https URL from a service the user signed in to, or a built-in one (Hugging Face), as the signed-in user when they are. The app attaches their secret; you never see it. Saves the body under scratch/api/<service>/ and returns status, type, size, the saved path and a short preview. A refusal that signing in would fix returns needs_signin. Hosts no sign-in covers are refused: fetch public data with the terminal.

url.description: The full https URL, with its query.

save_as.description: Optional file name for the saved body, e.g. 'train.parquet'.

function.name: propose_signin
function.description: Pause the run on a sign-in card when a service needs the user's sign-in for data they asked for: a built-in service by `provider`, or any other service by a `spec` you write from its API documentation. The app shows the spec (where the secret will be sent), draws the sign-in controls and checks the key; you give only the explanation and any steps the user takes on the service's site first. The run resumes once the user signs in or continues without.

provider.description: A built-in service. Use spec instead for any other.

spec.description: Any other service's sign-in, from its API documentation. Everything stays on one site: send_to hosts, get_token and check.

send_to.description: Exact API hosts the secret is sent to, e.g. ['www.kaggle.com']. No wildcards, ports or paths.

type.description: bearer: 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'; header: a named header; query: a named URL parameter; basic: HTTP basic with a username and key.

name.description: The header (header) or query parameter (query) that carries the secret.

username_label.description: basic: what the user types as the username, e.g. 'Account name'.

secret_label.description: What the user pastes, e.g. 'API key'.

get_token.description: The https page on the service's site where the user gets the secret.

instructions.description: What to do on that page, in a sentence or two.

check.description: Optional https URL on a send_to host that answers 2xx with a working secret; the app tries it before keeping the key.

local.description: Optional: how to read a login the user already has on this computer (e.g. from the service's CLI), offered on the card next to pasting a key. The card shows it as written; it runs only if the user picks it, then each time the sign-in is used. One of command, file or env.

command.description: Arguments, run without a shell; its output is the secret, e.g. ['gh', 'auth', 'token'].

file.description: A file holding the secret, e.g. '~/.kaggle/access_token'.

env.description: An environment variable holding the secret.

fields.description: When what is read is JSON: the secret's parts (token; or username and key for basic) mapped to their JSON keys, e.g. {'username': 'username', 'key': 'key'} for kaggle.json.

reason.description: Why: from needs_signin, or 'unauthorized' when the service requires a key, or 'other' when the user asked to sign in.

explanation.description: One or two sentences to the user: what you were doing and why the service refused or needs a sign-in.

unlocks.description: What signing in lets you do next, e.g. 'Download the Titanic competition's train.csv'.

steps.description: Steps on the service's own site, such as accepting a dataset's terms or a competition's rules.

url.description: A page on the service's own site (https).

prefer.description: Built-in services: the sign-in method to put first, if available.
